title: Bread with Lard, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Bread with lard in Puerto Rican style is a traditional snack consisting of soft white bread soaked in flavorful pork lard seasoned with typical Puerto Rican spices such as adobo, oregano, and garlic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in Puerto Rico in the early 20th century when Spanish colonists adapted local recipes using readily available pork lard.
The lard is often rendered until golden, giving the bread a crisp, buttery crust.
It is traditionally served with “mojo” sauce – a spicy tomato‑pepper sauce.
In Puerto Rico it is commonly eaten for breakfast or as a bar snack with beer.
Lard is considered an energy‑dense food and is often consumed during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: High energy source
items.content: Lard provides a large amount of calories, quickly replenishing energy stores.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 in pork lard is essential for nervous system function and blood formation.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Fatty acids for satiety
items.content: Saturated and monounsaturated fats in lard can promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Aids fat‑soluble vitamin absorption
items.content: The fats help absorb vitamins A, D, E, and K from other foods.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Overconsumption may lead to weight gain.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Frequent intake can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Lard is often salted; people with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to pork proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread is usually served warm, sliced. It can be spread on toast, added to sandwiches, or used as a base for toppings like mojo sauce, avocado, or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag where it retains flavor for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or skillet before serving.
